_doc: Applied by rewrite_past_perfect.py --apply-only after rewrite_pp_ok.json. 'items': locate the ORIGINAL string by its item location (from the scan) and apply each [old, new] substring once (must match exactly once). 'global': substring replacement in ANY string of the source JSONs (used for hints that explain the removed 'had').

replace: speech had won the class competition
every single visit had been deeply
the last box had been loaded
We had lived in the same block (4)________ I was five years old, so leaving it felt strange.
This has been our home (4)________ I was five years old, so leaving it felt strange.
When I came downstairs at seven, she had (7)________ arranged all the kitchen cupboards.
By seven the next morning, she was (7)________ done with all the kitchen cupboards.
Father, however, had not found his reading glasses (8)________
Father, however, could not find his reading glasses (8)________

global: It must be a past verb, because 'had first' comes in front of it.
It must be a past-tense verb, because the story is told in the past.
It follows 'had', so use the past participle.
The sentence is in the past, so use the past-tense form.
Father HAD NOT FOUND his READING GLASSES
Father COULD NOT FIND his READING GLASSES
The cupboards were done WHEN I CAME DOWNSTAIRS AT SEVEN
The cupboards were done BY SEVEN THE NEXT MORNING
